summary: write::incremental_update writes a replacement stream's dictionary as handed, so a /Length that does not count the bytes it writes is written beside them. A stream whose file stated /Length 3 over 15 bytes (read by endstream, logged STREAM_EXTENT_FROM_ENDSTREAM) and is handed back with one entry added is appended as '/Length 3' over the 15 bytes. serialize and linearize re-derive /Length from the bytes and count the disagreement (Written::relengthed); the incremental writer does neither for an unencrypted target (encryption.rs's encrypt_for_update re-derives it only when it encrypts). pdf-transform's insert-pages carry (update.rs Carry::value) copies an incoming document's stream dictionary with its own /Length beside data already out of §7.6's encryption, so an AES-encrypted incoming document's ciphertext /Length is written over the shorter plaintext on the same path.
source: ISO 32000-2 §7.3.8.2: "Every stream dictionary shall have a Length entry that indicates how many bytes of the PDF file are used for the stream's data." Table 5 /Length: "The number of bytes from the beginning of the line following the keyword stream to the last byte just before the keyword endstream." §7.3.8.1: "the stream dictionary specifies the exact number of bytes."
code: crates/pdf-syntax/src/write.rs:113-118 (write::object's Stream arm writes stream.dict then stream.data) and :362-376 (incremental_update_extending writes each replacement through object()); contrast serialize.rs:1740-1747 and linearize.rs:2739-2745; crates/pdf-transform/src/update.rs:1043-1053 (Carry::value copies the incoming dictionary)
change: Re-derive /Length as a direct integer from the bytes written for every stream an incremental update writes, as serialize and linearize do, and count the disagreements for the caller.
execution: FAIL (expected): crates/pdf-syntax/tests/objects_7_3_spec_audit.rs::an_incremental_update_states_the_length_of_the_bytes_it_writes_spec_audit — round 2243: /Length Some(3) over 15 bytes written; its control (a right /Length kept) passes.
status: fixed (ADR 3681; write::incremental_update re-derives every stream's /Length from the bytes it writes; objects_7_3_spec_audit::an_incremental_update_states_the_length_of_the_bytes_it_writes_spec_audit passes, and pdf-transform tests/update.rs carries a page out of an AES-256 source into a clear and an encrypted destination)

summary: A stream written as a direct value — `<< /Inner << /Length 3 >> stream ... endstream >>` — is read as a Stream value of the outer dictionary (or array) and nothing is logged: parse_dictionary_or_stream accepts the `stream` keyword after any dictionary at any depth. The file breaks §7.3.8.1, so the reading is a repair, and it is a silent one (no RepairClass), which ADR 3477 makes a finding. The writers then carry the direct stream out: write::object writes a Stream nested in a dictionary or array inline, and serialize's renumber keeps it nested with its /Length not re-derived (only a top-level stream's is), so a file this program writes repeats the malformation.
source: ISO 32000-2 §7.3.8.1: "All streams shall be indirect objects (see 7.3.10, \"Indirect objects\") and the stream dictionary shall be a direct object." §7.3.7: "An indirect reference (see 7.3.10, \"Indirect objects\") shall be used as the value to refer to a stream object"; §7.3.6 the same of an array's elements.

change: Read the stream keyword as a stream only at an indirect object's top level (or log a named repair class where a nested one is kept), and have the writers hoist or refuse a nested stream rather than write it inline.

summary: `/A#00B` writes character code 0 into a name through the number-sign escape; Lexer::read_name expands it into the name's bytes and logs nothing, though §7.3.5 defines a name as a sequence of any characters except null. The malformed name reaches every dictionary reader as an ordinary key or value, and Name::escaped writes it back out as #00. A silent repair under ADR 3477.
source: ISO 32000-2 §7.3.5: "Beginning with PDF 1.2 a name object is an atomic symbol uniquely defined by a sequence of any characters (8-bit values) except null (character code 0)." "Even though a name may contain any characters except null"

change: Log a named repair class (or refuse the token) when an escape decodes to 00h, and say in read_name's comment which reading the reader takes.

summary: Errata issue #379's published grammar makes an object number `1-9` followed by digits and a generation number `0` or `1-9` followed by digits — no sign, no leading zero. `+1 0 R`, `01 0 R` and `1 00 R` are each read as a reference with nothing logged; doc/errata-read.md's #379 row records the tolerance as undocumented and owed. Under ADR 3581 the erratum is the standard, so the reading is a repair, and a silent one.

summary: A script that sets a field's textSize (and not textFont) has the producer's /DA font restated in a new Tf, and that name is written raw after a lossy UTF-8 decode: a /DR key `Helv Bold` (written /Helv#20Bold) becomes `/Helv#20Bold 10 Tf 0 g /Helv Bold 14 Tf` — the name Helv, an operator Bold, and a Tf whose first operand is a number. A name byte above 7Fh becomes U+FFFD's three bytes. variable_text.rs writes the same operand through Name::escaped (ADR 0453); scripted_appearance is the route that does not.
source: ISO 32000-2 §7.3.5: "c) Any character that is not a regular character shall be written using its 2-digit hexadecimal code, preceded by the NUMBER SIGN only." "Whitespace used as part of a name shall always be coded using the 2-digit hexadecimal notation." "Regular characters that are outside the range EXCLAMATION MARK(21h) (!) to TILDE (7Eh) (~) should be written using the hexadecimal notation."

summary: variable_text's /DA replay narrows every real operand to f32 before writing it, so a real past f32's range — `400000000000000000000000000000000000000.5 w`, fixed-format syntax §7.3.3 admits, Annex C's limits being informative — is written into the field's appearance stream as `inf w`: not a number but an operator token, which leaves the w with no operand and adds an unknown operator. A real inside the range is also written at f32 precision, not 'in the syntax it came in' as the function says.
source: ISO 32000-2 §7.3.3: "A real value shall be written as one or more decimal digits with an optional sign and a leading, trailing, or embedded PERIOD (2Eh) (decimal point)." "A PDF writer shall not use the PostScript language syntax for numbers with non-decimal radices (such as 16#FFFE) or in exponential format (such as 6.02E23)."
